name: Wilkinson Sword

card.summary: A British razor brand (Quattro, Hydro, double-edge blades) used for shaving a clean, even face and neck.
card.aka: Wilkinson Sword razors; Schick (in other markets)
card.note: Razors can cause nicks, razor burn and ingrown hairs.

quick.overview:
Wilkinson Sword is a British brand with origins in gun and sword making that became a major maker of razors and blades. Today it sells multi-blade cartridge razors and double-edge safety razor blades.

For looks, a clean shave or a well-kept neckline is a basic grooming step; the brand is one option among many. Forum users mention Wilkinson double-edge blades as a common choice, while the company's Quattro and Hydro cartridges target mainstream shavers.
quick.how: Users either buy cartridge razors from the Quattro or Hydro lines or pair a double-edge safety razor with Wilkinson blades, along with a brush and soap or cream. The blades are replaced as they dull.
quick.risks: Shaving can cause nicks, razor burn, irritation and ingrown hairs, and technique and blade sharpness matter. Sharp blades should be stored and disposed of carefully.

lead: Wilkinson Sword is a British brand founded as a gunmaking business in 1772 by Henry Nock, later famous for swords and, from the late nineteenth century, a producer of razors. It is today owned by Edgewell Personal Care, and in some markets its razors are sold alongside Schick.[1][2]

In grooming, the brand supplies both multi-blade cartridge razors and double-edge safety razor blades. Wilkinson introduced stainless steel razor blades in the 1960s, launched the four-blade Quattro in 2003 and the Hydro system in 2010.[2]
Forum discussions of wet shaving sometimes name Wilkinson Sword among preferred double-edge blades, next to other brands.[3][4]

chain: Razor and blades remove facial and body hair
angle.text: A razor lets people keep a clean shave or define a neckline and beard edges. Wilkinson Sword is one brand of cartridges and double-edge blades for that purpose.

paras: Henry Nock founded the business in 1772 as a gunmaker. It later became James Wilkinson and Son and, in 1891, the Wilkinson Sword Company.[2]

The company introduced stainless steel razor blades in 1962 according to Wikipedia, whereas Grokipedia gives 1956.[2][1] A series of acquisitions followed, including Warner-Lambert in 1992 (forming Schick-Wilkinson Sword) and Energizer in 2003; the Quattro was introduced in 2003 and the Hydro on 6 April 2010. Edgewell took over personal care in 2015.[2]

On T Nation, users discussing razors describe using Wilkinson Sword double-edge blades in safety razors, one calling it a closer shave than disposable blades and another naming it among blades they like.[3][4]
As with any razor, shaving may cause cuts, irritation and ingrown hairs, and results depend on technique and skin type.

timeline.event: Henry Nock founds the business as a gunmaker.[2]
Stainless steel razor blades introduced (per Wikipedia).[2]
Energizer acquires the brand; Quattro four-blade razor launched.[2]
Edgewell Personal Care takes ownership via Energizer spin-off.[2]
